limitations: Identities are declared agent names plus hashed session ids, not signatures; a forger with write access can fabricate consistent files. Since D-26 such a forgery cannot reach a terminal project status: only the release check (re-execution and ablation at HEAD) gives one.

The interpreter's own files (standard library, installed packages) are trusted; a poisoned site-packages without a new start-up hook is not detected. Run the release check in an environment installed from requirements.lock.txt.

Static detection has limits: registry insertions paired with a removal count as negative controls; constants laundered through another module or arbitrary computation, recorded after a call of the implementation, pass both the static detector and the ablation. Ablation shows dependence on the implementation, not that the right property is measured; requirements whose implementation lists no Python module are not ablated.
The foreign-module rule rejects gate tests that import code they generated outside the clone (none of the current gate tests does).

--verify-all without --reproduce never reports a terminal status (it adds a project problem saying so); progress milestones therefore always record IN_PROGRESS until the release check.

A gate test whose evidence must verify: produced in its canonical gate file; no conftest on its path with outcome-rewriting hooks or patches; no imports from outside the clone; its measurement must not survive ablation of the listed implementation modules (a test that only reads constant tables of its implementation will be rejected).

Requirement changes: requirements.py is imported by every gate test (through checker.unmet and evidence), so adding or changing requirements makes all existing evidence stale (unchanged behaviour, now stated): settle requirements.py before producing official evidence.
